content.title: Lakers vs. Rockets: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/18/26)
content.text: The Los Angeles Lakers (43–25) face the Houston Rockets (41–26) tonight at the Toyota Center in Houston in their second matchup this week. Los Angeles won Monday’s matchup 100–92, powered by Luka Doncic’s 36-point performance as the Lakers extended their winning streak to six games. The Lakers currently sit third in the Western Conference, 10.5 games behind first place — a gap that appears difficult to close. More immediately, they hold just a 1.5-game cushion over the Rockets, Denver Nuggets, and Minnesota Timberwolves in a tightly contested race for the No. 3 through No. 6 seeds. Monday’s game was closely fought throughout, featuring 13 lead changes and neither team building a double-digit advantage. The Lakers ultimately secured the win with fourth-quarter defense, holding Houston to just 12 points while scoring 17 themselves. Austin Reaves struggled from beyond the arc, missing all eight of his three-point attempts and finishing with 15 points. LeBron James added 18. Houston also had difficulty from long range, shooting just 19% from deep. In the loss, Jabari Smith Jr. led the Rockets with 22 points, Amen Thompson added 19, and Kevin Durant scored 18. Houston played without Alperen Sengun in that contest, a significant absence in the frontcourt. He will return tonight. Expect another tightly contested matchup. But with Sengun back in the lineup, the edge shifts slightly toward Houston at home. Prediction: Houston Rockets 114, Los Angeles Lakers 109 Injury Report Los Angeles Lakers Maxi Kleber — Out (Back) Houston Rockets Jae’Sean Tate — Out (Knee) Steven Adams — Out For Season (Ankle) Fred VanVleet — Out (Knee) How to Watch Lakers vs. Rockets Tip-off for tonight’s Lakers-Rockets game is set for 9:30 PM Eastern / 8:30 PM Central / 6:30 PM Pacific at the Toyota Center in Houston. The game airs live on ESPN and streams on the ESPN app and website. If you’re a cord-cutter without an active livestreaming plan, you can watch the game for free by taking advantage of free trials from DIRECTV STREAM, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo TV, or YouTube TV. Fubo TV and Hulu + Live TV include ESPN Unlimited as part of their standard plans. Tonight’s game also airs live locally on SportsNet in L.A.
